items.title: Housing cash on the way after ‘speed lobbying’ sessions in Ottawa: Mississauga mayor
items.summary: A whirlwind visit to Ottawa this week has secured for Mississauga — and Peel Region — some much-needed cash for housing from the provincial government, the city’s mayor says. While not revealing the specific amount of funding headed to Mississauga and Peel, Mayor Carolyn Parrish said on Tuesday the City of Mississauga’s delegation was “well received” at the 2026 Association of Municipalities of Ontario conference. Mississauga Deputy Mayor and Ward 8 Coun. Matt Mahoney, Ward 3 Coun. Chris Fonseca, City Manager Geoff Wright and other members of the city’s senior leadership team joined Parrish in meeting with Ontario cabinet ministers, opposition party leaders, MPPs and industry stakeholders to discuss and advocate for Mississauga’s priorities. ” City of Mississauga officials, including Mayor Carolyn Parrish, met this week with various provincial cabinet ministers in Ottawa. (Photo: City of Mississauga) Beyond affordable housing, other priorities tabled by Mississauga’s delegation this week included strengthening public transit, supporting economic growth and trade resilience, addressing flood prevention and infrastructure needs, securing a fair police funding formula in Peel, and investing in arts, culture and sport infrastructure, city officials said. In addition, city officials also raised the matter of safety related to the use of electric scooters in Mississauga — an issue of concern that’s been discussed many times at city council the past two years.

items.title: Mississauga bets on its film industry as U.S. incentives grow
items.summary: From peameal bacon to a dim sum drag brunch, our food report… Starting Aug. S. incentives lure productions south. CBS Stages Canada at 1850 Matheson Blvd. E. As growing competition from jurisdictions across the United States puts pressure on Ontario’s film and television industry, Mississauga is doubling down on its identity as a production hub, advancing new initiatives to strengthen its footprint in the creative sector. Mississauga is home to eight major film studios with more than 1 million square feet of stage space. The city earned close to $1 million in revenue from film and television production in 2021 and described “film-related activity” as an important contributor to Mississauga’s economy. While the municipality is taking steps to strengthen its local production ecosystem, industry officials say the broader competitive landscape will also be shaped by policies and investment at the provincial and federal levels. In June 2026, city council adopted “The Creative Advantage: A Transformational Action Plan for Mississauga’s Cultural and Creative Sector,” a strategy aimed at increasing Mississauga’s appeal to creative businesses and investment, including those in the film industry.

items.title: Mississauga launches replica of Avro Arrow CF-105 at Paul Coffey Park
items.summary: The project commemorates a supersonic jet that was designed and built in the 1950s in Malton. Entertainment and activities | August 19, 2026 The City of Mississauga, in partnership with the Malton Business Improvement Area (BIA), invites the community to attend an exciting unveiling of a replica of the Avro Arrow CF-105 (RL-201), which was permanently installed in the Flight Garden located within Paul Coffey Park. Join Mayor Carolyn Parrish, Ward 5 Councillor Natalie Hart, Members of Council, Sam Kohli, Chair, Malton BIA, project sponsors and other special guests for a commemorative outdoor ceremony that will include the official unveiling of the Avro Arrow. Additional event details can be found below. Paul Coffey Park (Flight Garden) 6990 Goreway Dr. Mississauga, ON L4T 1A9 Mayor Carolyn Parrish Ward 5 Councillor, Natalie Hart Members of Council Sam Kohli, Chair, Malton BIA Project sponsors and special guests The project commemorates a supersonic jet that was designed and built in the 1950s in Mississauga’s Malton neighbourhood. Impressively, the original Avro Arrow was the largest plane of its kind when built, measuring 55 feet wide and 72 feet long. The Arrow included many firsts: digital computers and computer numerical control machining were used in the design and components; computer-controlled navigation, weapons release, electronic counter measures and jamming technology. In its time, the jet had superior speed, lower weight and the ability to carry more payloads. For more information, view the event calendar listing.

items.title: CIK Telecom Expands SuperFibre to 5,000 More Mississauga Condo Units
items.summary: CIK Telecom is celebrating its 23rd anniversary and announced that its high-speed SuperFibre Internet service is now available in more than 5,000 additional condominium units across Mississauga, Ontario, following network upgrades completed in the first half of 2026. The expansion reflects the company's continued investment in fibre infrastructure and its commitment to delivering fast, reliable, and affordable connectivity to Canadian households. With this latest expansion, CIK's SuperFibre network now covers all buildings in the area surrounding Square One in Mississauga, further strengthening its fibre network presence in the heart of the city. The newly connected developments span several of Mississauga's fastest-growing residential communities, enabling thousands of residents to access ultra-fast, reliable fibre Internet. CIK's SuperFibre service is designed to support today's connected lifestyles, including remote work, HD and 4K streaming, online gaming, video conferencing, and smart home applications. Driving Affordability and Consumer Choice As Internet affordability remains a growing concern for Canadian households, CIK Telecom continues to expand access to competitively priced fibre services that deliver high performance without premium pricing. By investing in network growth and service innovation, the company aims to provide consumers with more competitive alternatives while contributing to a healthier telecommunications marketplace in Canada. Supporting Mississauga’s Growing Communities Mississauga is one of Canada's fastest-growing cities, with significant residential development continuing across the region. By deploying SuperFibre in both newly constructed and existing residential buildings, CIK is ensuring that residents have access to the modern connectivity needed to support work, education, entertainment, and everyday digital living.

items.title: Is Heated Rivalry season 2 filming at this Mississauga ice rink?
items.summary: Filming for season two of the viral Canadian queer series Heated Rivalry is underway, and some have rumoured that a film set close to home may be part of the production. In an Instagram post on Monday, the team behind the popular hockey show posted a picture of a film slate in front of what seemed to be a potential scene in the upcoming season. The description “Day 1” confirmed to fans that production behind the series has begun, possibly on Monday. A post shared by Heated Rivalry (@heatedrivalryhq) And while the Heated Rivalry buzz has returned, Torontonians and Mississauga residents noticed there may have been a production filming at an Olympic-sized ice rink in the west end city, which would possibly correlate with the hockey show’s filming schedule. Filming Update! A Mystery Production has been spotted filming at Iceland Mississauga TODAY. 🤔🎥🎬 Hmmmm… First day of filming on #HeatedRivalry S2, and now we’ve got a production filming at a hockey rink. Could it be? com/AgBBLwxq2i While there is no confirmation of what the production was at Iceland Mississauga nor if it was a taping of Heated Rivalry, a customer service representative at the arena confirmed to Now Toronto over the phone that there was a production filming on location on Aug. 17. Unfortunately, the representative added that staff do not have information on bookings at the arena, and scheduling of the space comes from a third party organization. The hockey show was also not listed as a production currently being shot in Mississauga, according to the film and industry website Production List.

items.title: Peel police sign 'first-of-its-kind' pact with Human Rights Commission to implement dozens of anti-racism recommendations
items.summary: The agreement will see a new independent oversight process to help drive “meaningful, measurable change” against systemic racism. Peel Regional Police Chief Nishan Duraiappah lauded the agreement as a concrete step in building trust with residents. The force started consultations to help address systemic racism back in 2020. A new independent body will be tasked with guiding the implementation of more than 65 recommendations to address systemic racism within Peel police, after a “first-of-its-kind” agreement was struck between the service, its board and the Ontario Human Rights Commission (OHRC). The binding arbitration accord, announced Tuesday, aims to enact a wide range of recommendations to eliminate racial discrimination, such as the further prohibition of police street checks and carding the use of de-escalation techniques, and emphasizing organizational change through hiring and training. ” “Policing must be fair, equitable, and free from systemic bias. This first-of-its-kind agreement demonstrates our leadership in driving meaningful, measurable change through transparent, independent oversight,” he said in a statement. The three organizations say the recommendations were made by the OHRC through the Human Rights Project, which began in February 2020.

items.title: Trapeze Duo Behind Canada's First Quadruple Somersault Set to Perform in Mississauga This Month
items.summary: According to INsauga, the Royal Canadian Circus is bringing a newly set Canadian first with it when it arrives in Mississauga this month, days after a milestone performance in Scarborough. Circus officials said trapeze duo The Flying Poema completed Canada's first-ever quadruple somersault during the closing weekend of a 10-day run at Scarborough Town Centre. INsauga reports officials described the move as an extremely rare feat that only a handful of performers worldwide have ever landed, and said The Flying Poema plans to attempt it again at future stops on the tour. The circus, currently marking its 52nd anniversary Canadian tour, will set up in the parking lot of Dixie Outlet Mall in Mississauga's east end from August 21 to 30, following a similar 10-day stay at the same mall in August 2025. INsauga notes the Mississauga stop is part of an all-new 2026 production that has already toured through Hamilton, Brampton, Newmarket, Markham and Vaughan, with Burlington next up on the schedule from September 3 to 7.

items.title: Studio.89 Will Shut Its Eglinton Avenue Storefront But Keep Its Community Programs Running
items.summary: According to INsauga, Studio.89, a non-profit fair trade and vegan cafe that has also served as a community hub in Mississauga, announced on Instagram that it will close its brick-and-mortar location on September 14. INsauga reports the cafe has operated at 2520 Eglinton Avenue West, offering espresso drinks, coffee, smoothies, sandwiches and treats as a social enterprise that funnels sales toward its social, cultural and environmental mission. This isn't the first time the organization has faced a financial crunch, INsauga notes, pointing to a 2018 fundraising push that brought in a $50,000 donation to help keep the cafe's doors open. Even after the physical space closes, Studio.89 says it plans to keep running its community programming at venues across Mississauga, according to INsauga. Those programs include initiatives focused on art as a tool for social change, climate action, youth leadership, connections between youth and seniors, and job skills training.

items.title: Chef Matty Matheson's Maker Pizza Chain Set to Open Its Fifth Location in Mississauga
items.summary: According to WhatNow, Maker Pizza, the pizza chain founded by celebrity chef Matty Matheson and business partner Shlomo Buchler, is set to open a new location at 181 City Centre Drive in Mississauga in late August. WhatNow reports the Mississauga shop will mark the brand's fifth location since it launched in 2015 with an original spot on Cameron Street. The new store joins existing Maker Pizza locations on Cameron Street, Bayview Avenue and Carlaw Avenue in Toronto, along with a Bathurst Street shop in Thornhill. According to the report, the menu sells pizza by the slice or whole pie, with specialty options including Siena Margherita, Napoli Dynamite, Dr. Pepperoni and Tropic Thunder. WhatNow notes the shop also offers a range of dips, such as creamy garlic, dill ranch and spicy creamy garlic, along with wings and garlic fingers.

items.title: Independent Verifier Will Check Whether Peel Police Follows Through on Anti-Racism Recommendations
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police will now face independent oversight to verify whether it is actually carrying out recommendations meant to eliminate racial profiling and systemic discrimination within the force. INsauga reports the new agreement between Peel Regional Police, the Peel Police Services Board and the Ontario Human Rights Commission sets up a process to check on implementation and resolve disputes between the three parties, including through binding arbitration if needed. The recommendations trace back to a Human Rights Project the three organizations launched in 2020, which involved consultations with Black, Indigenous and other racialized communities and led to an initial set of recommendations released in 2023. According to INsauga, those recommendations are built on seven principles developed by the OHRC, covering areas such as acknowledging systemic racism, community engagement, policy changes, accountability, organizational change and data collection. Under the new agreement, the three organizations will jointly select an independent verifier, with support from the community-based Anti-Racism Advisory Committee, to assess the department's progress, INsauga notes.

items.title: 2 online child luring police investigations lead to multiple charges for Mississauga man
items.summary: A Mississauga man faces multiple charges in connection with two online child sexual abuse investigations conducted by different police forces. York Regional Police said on Tuesday that investigators with the police agency’s Internet Child Exploitation unit laid a number of child sexual abuse and exploitation material charges as part of an ongoing investigation. Police said their probe began in September 2025 when officers started looking into a suspect who was using an online platform to arrange meetings with youths he believed were under the age of 16 for the purpose of committing sexual offences. “Over the span of seven months, the suspect continued to send messages using numerous aliases including ‘Scanner’, ‘Competentist’, ‘James Thomas’, ‘JP T’ and ‘Confessionator’,” York police said in a news release issued Tuesday. Investigators in York were then notified in May by Ontario Provincial Police who were investigating “similar allegations involving the same suspect and motive,” police said. A man was arrested in June in relation to both investigations. John Thompson, 52, of Mississauga, is charged with: John Thompson, 52, of Mississauga.
